verdict.summary: Create one OAuth app and have each customer connect their own Dropbox account. After 50 users link the app, submit it for production review. Dropbox generally handles production requests in a few business days, based on an old community reply.
verdict.activeEffort: 3–6 hours, mostly configuring OAuth and preparing production materials
verdict.waitTime: A few business days after submitting a production request (community-reported; not an SLA)
verdict.mainGate: Dropbox will not review a production request until 50 Dropbox users link the app. After reaching 50 users, you must apply for and receive production approval within two weeks or new user linking freezes.

recommendation.text: Create one Dropbox API app for your product. Use authorization-code OAuth for every customer's account. Choose App Folder access unless the agent needs files outside its own folder.

sources.quote: use one and exactly one key for each app you make
The code flow is the recommended OAuth flow for all types of applications.
App Folder: Your application will be able to take actions allowed by its scopes on data within its app folder only

scopeTiers.text: This is the cheapest read-only tier. Dropbox has no separate scope review tier. Production review remains app-level.

sources.quote: Your app should use the least privileged permission it can.
it will not be reviewed until your app has linked with at least 50 Dropbox users

scopeTiers.need: Read the customer's account details, file names, and file contents.

scopeTiers.text: This adds file changes. Dropbox still performs one app-level production review.

sources.quote: /files/upload files.content.write
Your app will undergo a production readiness review by Dropbox and will either be approved or denied.

scopeTiers.need: Read files and create or update files.

scopeTiers.text: This adds shared-item actions. Use it only when the agent creates or manages sharing links.

sources.quote: "scope": "files.content.read files.metadata.read sharing.read sharing.write",
Your app should use the least privileged permission it can.

scopeTiers.need: Read files and create or manage shared links.

essentials.text: Request offline access with token_access_type=offline. Store the reusable refresh token encrypted. Refresh at /oauth2/token with grant_type=refresh_token. Use the returned expiry instead of a fixed lifetime.

sources.quote: you’ll need to include token_access_type=offline as a parameter on your Authorization URL in order to return a refresh_token
The refresh token can be repeatedly re-used and doesn't expire automatically (though it can be revoked on demand).
Once the current short-lived access token expires, call the /oauth2/token endpoint with the refresh token to get a new short-lived access token
Dropbox access tokens are short lived, and will expire after a short period of time.

essentials.text: Register every callback URL in the Developer Console. Send the exact registered URL in each authorization request. Dropbox rejects callback URLs outside this list.

sources.quote: You’ll need to register the exact redirect URI(s) your app may use in the Developer Console for your application.
Redirection to any URI not specified here will not be allowed.

essentials.text: New apps start in development status. Enable additional users for testing. Development apps can link up to 500 Dropbox users.

sources.quote: By default, all apps are created in the development state, which limits the total number of users who can access your app during early development.
Clicking ‘Enable additional users’ will allow a limited number of additional users to link to you application for testing or internal use.
it can only be linked with up to 500 total Dropbox users

essentials.text: Queue work separately for each connected account or team. Exact limits are unpublished. On HTTP 429, wait for the Retry-After value before retrying.

sources.quote: The Dropbox API enforces rate limits on the number of API calls issued over a period of time on a per-authorization basis
Rate limited responses always include a Retry-After header
While Dropbox does not publish exact rate limits

essentials.text: Not found in the sources researched.
Production approval removes the user linking cap. Lock the app name before approval, because Dropbox does not allow later name changes.

sources.quote: Once your app is approved for production status, any number of Dropbox users can link to your app.
once your app has production status, you can’t change its name

essentials.text: Request production status with Apply for production in the Developer Console. Review begins only after 50 users link the app. Add an icon, explain API use, and provide an app-specific privacy policy.

sources.quote: When you’re ready to release your app publicly, you can request a review by clicking the Apply for production button.
it will not be reviewed until your app has linked with at least 50 Dropbox users
Before you apply, add an app icon on your app’s Branding tab.
Be sure to include a clear privacy policy that’s specific to your app

essentials.text: Use HTTPS and reasonable safeguards for user data and tokens. Do not collect Dropbox passwords. Ask for only the permissions needed for the requested agent action.

sources.quote: prevent loss, theft, damage, or unauthorized access to or disclosure of User Data and access tokens using no less than reasonable security measures
use secure communication protocols such as SSL or TLS and Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure (HTTPS) enabled by default
Developer will promptly delete login credentials once the User has completed the initial authentication
Your app should use the least privileged permission it can.

requests.text: Direct the user here to authorize offline access with PKCE.

sources.quote: https://www.dropbox.com/oauth2/authorize?client_id=<APP KEY>&response_type=code&token_access_type=offline&state=<STATE>&redirect_uri=<REDIRECT URI>
Include a code_challenge_method and code_challenge in your authorization URL. The code challenge method may be S256 or plain. Using S256 is the recommended approach.
https://www.dropbox.com/oauth2/authorize?client_id=YOUR_CLIENT_ID&redirect_uri=YOUR_REDIRECT_URI&response_type=code& scope=files.content.read&account_info.read

requests.label: Send the user to sign in

requests.text: Exchange the one-time authorization code for a short-lived access token and refresh token.

sources.quote:
curl https://api.dropbox.com/oauth2/token \
-d code=<AUTHORIZATION CODE> \
-d grant_type=authorization_code \
-d client_id=<APP KEY> \
-d client_secret=<APP SECRET> \
-d redirect_uri=<REDIRECT URI>
In your request to the /oauth2/token endpoint, pass the code_verifier with your generated value instead of the client_id.

requests.label: Exchange the code for tokens
requests.curl:
curl https://api.dropbox.com/oauth2/token \
  -d code=AUTH_CODE \
  -d grant_type=authorization_code \
  -d code_verifier=CODE_VERIFIER \
  -d redirect_uri=YOUR_REDIRECT_URI

requests.text: Use the refresh token to obtain a new short-lived access token.

sources.quote:
curl https://api.dropbox.com/oauth2/token \
-d refresh_token=<REFRESH TOKEN> \
-d grant_type=refresh_token \
-d client_id=<APP KEY> \
-d client_secret=<APP SECRET>

requests.label: Refresh the access token
requests.curl:
curl https://api.dropbox.com/oauth2/token \
  -d refresh_token=REFRESH_TOKEN \
  -d grant_type=refresh_token \
  -d client_id=YOUR_CLIENT_ID \
  -d client_secret=YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET

requests.text: Retrieve the currently connected Dropbox account.

sources.quote:
curl -X POST https://api.dropboxapi.com/2/users/get_current_account \
--header "Authorization: Bearer <ACCESS TOKEN>"

requests.label: Check the connection

requests.text: Revoke the access token and its corresponding refresh token.

sources.quote: Apps can revoke an access token (and corresponding refresh token, if any) using the /2/auth/token/revoke endpoint.
This access token can be used by your app in subsequent API calls for that user. It should be passed with the Authorization HTTP header value of Bearer <oauth2-access-token>

requests.label: Revoke access

detail.text: Sign in to the Developer Console and create one app. Choose the API, access type, and app name. Use App Folder access unless your product needs the customer's wider Dropbox.

sources.quote: It walks you through three steps: choose an API, choose the type of access you need, and name your app.
App Folder: Your application will be able to take actions allowed by its scopes on data within its app folder only

detail.text: Open Permissions and select the smallest scopes your agent needs. Open Settings and register each exact callback URL. This limits data access and prevents unlisted callbacks.

sources.quote: Each app in the Developer Console is broken into four primary sections: Settings, Permissions, Branding, and Analytics.
The Dropbox API uses OAuth scopes to determine the actions your application is allowed to perform on a user’s data.
You’ll need to register the exact redirect URI(s) your app may use in the Developer Console for your application.

detail.text: Use code flow at the Dropbox authorization endpoint. Send a session-bound state value and token_access_type=offline. Validate state, then exchange the code at /oauth2/token and encrypt the refresh token.

sources.quote: The code flow is the recommended OAuth flow for all types of applications.
If your application needs additional context to complete the redirect, you may pass a state parameter the authorization URL - which will be returned as a query parameter in the redirect.
Call the /oauth2/token endpoint with your app’s client_secret to exchange the code for an access token in order to make API calls

steps.title: Draft reviewer API explanation

detail.text: Adapt this draft for the production form. Replace the generic product description with your actual features. Explain every requested permission.

sources.quote: you’ll be prompted to supply additional information such as how your app uses the API
use and disclose User Data only as authorized by the User and only as necessary for the functionality of the Developer App.

steps.output: Our agent connects only after a user authorizes Dropbox. It reads requested files to answer that user's request. It requests only account, metadata, and content read permissions. Write access is requested only when the user asks the agent to create or update a file. We store refresh tokens encrypted. We do not collect Dropbox passwords. Users can disconnect their Dropbox account from our product.

detail.text: Keep the app in development status. Click Enable additional users for internal testers. Do not exceed 500 linked Dropbox users before production approval.

sources.quote: Clicking ‘Enable additional users’ will allow a limited number of additional users to link to you application for testing or internal use.
it can only be linked with up to 500 total Dropbox users

detail.text: Test expired access tokens, revoked connections, and HTTP 429 responses. Refresh access tokens when needed. Queue calls per connected account and honor Retry-After.

sources.quote: it will not be reviewed until your app has linked with at least 50 Dropbox users
once your app links 50 Dropbox users, you will have two weeks to apply for and receive production status approval

detail.text: Wait for Dropbox to approve or deny the production request. Dropbox said it generally handles production requests within a few business days. This is an old community report, not a service commitment.

sources.quote: We generally get to all production requests within a few business days.

detail.text: Update your TLS trust store and Dropbox SDK dependencies. Dropbox began changing its API server certificate root in 2026.

sources.quote: Dropbox API server certificates began transitioning to a new root on or after January 1, 2026.

gotchas.text: Do not use implicit OAuth flow for a new agent. It cannot return refresh tokens for offline work.

sources.quote: Dropbox continues to support this legacy flow for compatibility, but recommends PKCE for new apps.
The use of response_type=code is necessary for offline access; response_type=token does not support offline access.

gotchas.text: Production review only applies after 50 linked users. At 50 users, approval must arrive within two weeks or new linking freezes.
